title: Runbook: search-api high latency
text: Use when the search-api p95 latency alert fires. 1. Check the CDN cache hit rate dashboard. 2. Check pod CPU and scale out if above 70%. 3. Check recent deploys and roll back the last one if the timing matches. 4. If latency is still high, page the search team.

title: Runbook: rolling back a service deploy
text: Find the previous good version in the deploy log. Run `deployctl rollback <service> <version>`. Watch error rate and latency for 15 minutes. Record the rollback in the incident ticket.

title: Runbook: auth-gateway signing key and certificate rotation
text: Quarterly. 1. Generate the new key pair. 2. Publish the new public key to the JWKS endpoint. 3. Wait until every verifier pod reports the new key id. 4. Switch signing to the new key. If logins fail with 'invalid token signature', re-publish the JWKS and restart the verifier pods.

title: Runbook: checkout-api error spike
text: Check the payment and tax provider status pages. Check recent checkout-api deploys. Raise downstream timeouts only as a stopgap. Roll back if a deploy matches the start time.

title: Runbook: catalog indexing lag
text: Check the indexing queue depth. Add workers if the queue grows. Check batch size and write latency to the search index. Large batches can slow each write.

title: Runbook: GPU node capacity for model serving
text: Model-serving pods (rerankers, recommenders) run on the GPU node pool. If queue time rises, check GPU utilisation and batch sizes. Add nodes through the capacity request form; it takes about a day.

title: Runbook: CDN cache misses
text: If origin traffic jumps, check the CDN cache hit rate by path. Compare cache rules with the last known good config and roll back the CDN config change.

title: How to read weekly SLO reports
text: Each service gets a weekly report with p50, p95 and p99 latency, availability and error budget. A week that breaches the latency SLO needs an incident link in the review.

title: Runbook: turning off a feature flag
text: Use flagctl to turn a flag off for all users. Flags take effect within a minute. Record the change in the deploy log.

title: On-call handbook: first 15 minutes
text: Acknowledge the page. Open an incident ticket. Check dashboards, recent deploys and provider status. Mitigate first, find the root cause later.
